title: Orange County Commission, District 8 (runoff)
what_it_does: County commissioners set the county budget and property-tax (millage) rate, adopt land-use and zoning rules, and oversee county services such as roads, parks, libraries, fire/EMS and utilities. District 8 is a newly created seat in 2026.

candidates.name: Victor Torres
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: Retired New York City police detective and retired LYNX bus operator; former Florida state senator and state representative
candidates.background: Torres is a Marine Corps veteran, retired New York City detective and retired school bus and LYNX bus operator and union member. He was elected to the Florida House in 2012 and the state Senate in 2016, and was term-limited in 2024. He led the August 18, 2026 primary for the newly created Orange County Commission District 8 with more than 33% and faces Jeannette Quinones Hernandez in a November 3 runoff.
candidates.primary_result: First in Aug 18 primary with more than 33%

property_tax.quote: I cannot support a constitutional amendment that dramatically reduces local property tax revenue without a responsible plan to replace it.

candidates.name: Jeannette Quinones Hernandez
candidates.occupation: Former small business owner; outreach specialist in U.S. Sen. Marco Rubio's office
candidates.background: Quinones Hernandez is a mother and former small business owner who worked as an outreach specialist and coordinator in then-U.S. Sen. Marco Rubio's office. She finished second in the August 18, 2026 primary for the newly created Orange County Commission District 8 with about 20% and advanced to the November 3 runoff against Victor Torres. Her campaign emphasizes road congestion, flooding and lower taxes.
candidates.primary_result: Second in Aug 18 primary with nearly 20%

taxes.summary: She says property taxes are too high and that revenue lost to a tax cut should be replaced primarily through service efficiencies, cutting waste and prioritizing core government functions.
taxes.quote: primarily through service efficiencies, cutting waste, and prioritizing core government functions

sources.title: 2026 Voter's Guide - Orange County Commission District 8

property_tax.summary: She supports the proposed constitutional amendment to sharply cut property taxes, saying they are too high and burden homeowners, seniors on fixed incomes and working families, and that lost revenue should be replaced mainly through service efficiencies and cutting waste.
property_tax.quote: YES. Property taxes are too high and burden homeowners, seniors on fixed incomes, and working families.
